title: Masterpieces
description: The most iconic paintings of all time — start here.

items.title: Mona Lisa
items.description_narrative: The most famous painting in the world. It depicts Lisa Gherardini, wife of Francesco del Giocondo, sitting in front of an imaginary landscape. Her enigmatic expression and the masterful use of sfumato make it a masterpiece of the Renaissance.
items.tags: portrait, renaissance, sfumato, enigmatic, female
items.credit_line: C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition: image page

items.title: The Last Supper
items.description_narrative: Painted on the refectory wall of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, Leonardo captures the instant Christ announces that one of the Twelve Apostles will betray him, freezing each figure mid-reaction. Its rigorous perspective and psychological drama made it one of the most studied and reproduced compositions in Western art.
items.tags: renaissance, religious, fresco, italian, dramatic, iconic, milan

items.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei)"
items.description_narrative: Katsushika Hokusai's iconic color woodblock print, 'The Great Wave,' captures a colossal wave cresting over three fishing boats, threatening to engulf them amidst a turbulent sea. In the distance, the serene form of Mount Fuji stands against the sky, anchoring this dramatic scene from his famous series 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.'
items.tags: great wave, mount fuji, ukiyo-e, woodblock print, ocean, dramatic, japanese landscape
items.credit_line: Library of Congress Catalog: https://lccn.loc.gov/2008660568 Image download: https://cdn.loc.gov/service/pnp/jpd/02000/02018v.jpg Original url: https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/2008660568/

items.title: The Starry Night
items.description_narrative: A swirling, dynamic night sky over a quiet village, painted during Van Gogh's stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It is one of the most recognized masterpieces in the history of Western art.
items.tags: night, sky, stars, village, post-impressionism, landscape

items.title: The Scream
items.medium: Oil, tempera, pastel and crayon on cardboard
items.description_narrative: An agonized figure against a tumultuous orange sky, standing on a bridge. Widely interpreted as representing the universal anxiety of modern humanity. Munch described the inspiration as feeling an infinite scream passing through nature.
items.tags: scream, anxiety, expressionism, bridge, sunset, anguish
items.credit_line: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

items.title: Primavera
items.description_narrative: A procession of mythological figures - Venus, the Three Graces, Flora, and Mercury - drifts through an orange grove in one of the most celebrated allegories of the Florentine Renaissance. Botticelli's linear grace and flowering meadow have made it an emblem of Renaissance humanism.
items.tags: renaissance, mythology, allegory, florentine, springtime, elegant, botticelli

items.title: The Night Watch
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' depicts the company of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq and Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch moving out, renowned for its dramatic use of light and shadow. This monumental group portrait is a masterpiece of the Dutch Golden Age, celebrated for its dynamic composition and psychological depth.
items.tags: dutch golden age, group portrait, baroque, militia, dramatic, masterpiece, civic guard

items.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
items.description_narrative: Often referred to as the 'Mona Lisa of the North', this tronie depicts a European girl wearing an exotic dress, an oriental turban, and what appears to be a very large pearl as an earring. It is a masterclass in the use of light.
items.tags: portrait, dutch golden age, pearl, turban, female

items.title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I
items.medium: Oil, silver, and gold on canvas
items.description_narrative: Klimt envelops Viennese patron Adele Bloch-Bauer in shimmering, mosaic-like gold ornament, fusing Byzantine influence with Art Nouveau glamour. Later dubbed the "Woman in Gold" after a landmark restitution case, it remains Klimt's most celebrated portrait.
items.tags: vienna secession, gold leaf, portraiture, art nouveau, byzantine, symbolism

items.title: Water Lilies
items.description_narrative: Claude Monet's 'Water Lilies' captures the ephemeral play of light and reflection on the surface of his water garden at Giverny. This painting is part of an extensive series, through which Monet explored the subtle changes in nature across different times of day and seasons.
items.tags: water lilies, pond, nature, impressionism, french art, tranquil, reflections, garden
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Irises
items.description_narrative: Painted in the first week of van Gogh's stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, this study of the garden's flowerbed bursts with twisting blue-violet blooms against orange marigolds. Van Gogh considered it a calming color study, though it is now among his most reproduced paintings.
items.tags: van gogh, irises, saint-remy, asylum garden, flowers, post-impressionism, color
items.credit_line: DgFVFAJo_30MeQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Creation of Adam
items.description_narrative: The most famous section of the Sistine Chapel ceiling. God reaches out to give life to Adam, their fingers nearly touching. This single gesture has become one of the most replicated religious images and an enduring icon of humanity.
items.tags: fresco, sistine chapel, genesis, god, adam, renaissance
items.credit_line: Own work Burkhard Mücke Taken on 18 October 2017

items.title: American Gothic
items.description_narrative: A stern-faced farmer standing beside his spinster daughter in front of a house with a distinctive Gothic window. One of the most familiar images in 20th-century American art, it is an ambiguous statement about rural American character.
items.tags: portrait, american, gothic, rural, farmer, pitchfork
items.credit_line: Art Institute of Chicago: online database: entry 6565

items.title: Sunflowers
items.description_narrative: One of two series of sunflower still lifes by Van Gogh. Painted in Arles to decorate the room of his friend Paul Gauguin, the vivid yellows and expressive brushwork make this among the most recognizable still-life paintings in art history.
items.tags: sunflowers, still life, yellow, vase, post-impressionism

items.title: Olympia
items.description_narrative: Manet's reclining nude, a confrontational courtesan attended by a maid and a hissing black cat, upended the idealized Venuses of academic tradition when exhibited at the 1865 Salon. Its harsh lighting and unapologetic gaze made it one of the most controversial and influential paintings of the 19th century.
items.tags: manet, nude, courtesan, salon, controversy, paris, realism

items.title: The Birth of Venus
items.description_narrative: The goddess Venus emerges from the sea as a fully grown woman, arriving at the shore on a giant scallop shell. One of the world's most famous and appreciated works of art, it has become a landmark of Italian Renaissance painting.
items.tags: mythology, venus, renaissance, goddess, shell, classical

items.title: The Last Judgment
items.description_narrative: Covering the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel, Christ presides over the resurrection of the dead, the saved ascending and the damned cast down in a swirling mass of muscular bodies. Its sculptural intensity and unflinching nudity provoked controversy even as it cemented Michelangelo's reputation as the supreme master of the human form.
items.tags: renaissance, religious, fresco, sistine chapel, dramatic, monumental, michelangelo

items.title: Nighthawks
items.description_narrative: Four figures sit in a brightly lit diner at night on a desolate city corner. The painting captures the loneliness and alienation of modern urban life with cinematic intensity. It has become one of the most reproduced paintings in American art.
items.tags: diner, night, urban, loneliness, realism, american

items.title: Las Meninas
items.description_narrative: Velázquez places himself at his easel alongside the young Infanta Margarita Theresa and her attendants, while the king and queen appear only as reflections in a mirror. Its layered play of viewpoints and presence has made it one of the most analyzed paintings in Western art history.
items.tags: baroque, spanish, court, portrait, illusion, masterpiece, velazquez
items.credit_line: The Prado in Google Earth: Home page 7th level of zoom, JPEG compression quality: Photoshop 8.

items.title: View of Delft
items.description_narrative: Vermeer renders his native city across the Schie river beneath a dramatic sky of shifting light and cloud, its brick facades touched with small, luminous highlights. Marcel Proust famously called it "the most beautiful painting in the world," praising a tiny patch of yellow wall.
items.tags: dutch golden age, cityscape, luminous, delft, atmospheric, vermeer, sky

items.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
items.description_narrative: Renoir gathered his friends on a balcony overlooking the Seine at Chatou for this sunlit celebration of leisure, food, and conversation. The painting's loose brushwork and dappled light rank it among the most beloved images of Impressionist conviviality.
items.tags: impressionism, renoir, leisure, riverside, group portrait, sunlight
items.credit_line: mgHsTKDNJVzPAg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Luncheon on the Grass
items.description_narrative: Manet scandalized the 1863 Salon des Refusés by placing a nude woman among clothed men at a casual picnic, rejecting academic convention for blunt modern realism. Its flattened forms and startling frankness made it a touchstone for the Impressionist generation that followed.
items.tags: manet, realism, nude, picnic, scandal, modernity, paris
items.credit_line: twELHYoc3ID_VA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette
items.description_narrative: A lively Sunday afternoon crowd of dancers, drinkers, and socialites fills the open-air dance garden at the Moulin de la Galette in Montmartre. Praised for its dappled sunlight and sense of joyous movement, it is one of Impressionism's most celebrated works, now held at the Musée d'Orsay.
items.tags: Impressionism, Montmartre, dance, Paris, leisure, crowd scene
items.credit_line: rQEx7CtGiKE3yg at Google Cultural Institute zoom level scaled down from highest

items.title: The Kiss
items.medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
items.description_narrative: A couple locked in an intimate embrace, cloaked in elaborate gold-patterned robes, kneeling in a flower-strewn meadow. Klimt's masterful use of gold leaf and ornamental motifs epitomizes his 'Golden Phase' and the height of the Vienna Secession movement.
items.tags: love, gold, art nouveau, couple, embrace, ornamental

items.title: The Sleeping Gypsy
items.description_narrative: A lion sniffs a sleeping mandolin-player beside her water jug under a full moon in a silent moonlit desert. Rousseau's most hauntingly still, dreamlike scene, it was later revered by the Surrealists.
items.tags: dream, lion, desert, moonlight, naive art, surreal

items.title: The Bedroom (Amsterdam version, 1888)
items.description_narrative: The first of three versions van Gogh painted of his bedroom in the Yellow House in Arles, using flat planes of color to express restfulness. This original canvas is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: bedroom, yellow house, arles, interior, van gogh museum

items.title: The Hay Wain
items.description_narrative: Constable depicted a horse-drawn wagon fording the River Stour near his childhood home in Suffolk, capturing the changeable English sky and rural life with unprecedented naturalism. Poorly received in England at first, it won a gold medal in Paris and profoundly influenced French Romantic and Barbizon painters.
items.tags: constable, suffolk, countryside, river stour, romanticism, rural england

items.title: The Fighting Temeraire
items.description_narrative: A grand old warship that fought at Trafalgar is towed by a small, sooty steam tug to be broken up for scrap, its ghostly white sails glowing against a blazing sunset. Turner's elegy for the age of sail mourns the passing of a heroic era before industrial modernity.
items.tags: turner, warship, trafalgar, sunset, romanticism, steam tug, british navy

items.title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
items.description_narrative: Dr. Tulp demonstrates the tendons of a cadaver's forearm to a cluster of attentive surgeons, their varied expressions captured with a young Rembrandt's already remarkable psychological acuity. The group portrait broke from static convention, unifying the figures around a single dramatic action.
items.tags: dutch golden age, group portrait, anatomical, dramatic, amsterdam, rembrandt, scientific

items.title: The Art of Painting
items.description_narrative: An allegory of painting shows an artist at his easel before a model posed as Clio, the muse of history, in a light-filled studio hung with a map of the Netherlands. Vermeer never sold the work, keeping it as a showpiece of his art throughout his life.

items.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
items.description_narrative: In one of Rembrandt's final and most profound works, a ragged, kneeling son is embraced by his forgiving father as onlookers watch in silence. Painted in the last year of the artist's life, it distills a lifetime of psychological insight into the biblical parable of unconditional forgiveness.
items.tags: biblical parable, forgiveness, father and son, late Rembrandt, Hermitage, emotion

items.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
items.description_narrative: A merchant and his wife stand hand in hand in a richly furnished chamber, a convex mirror on the back wall reflecting the room and two additional figures in the doorway. Dense with symbolic detail, from the single candle to the small dog, it remains one of the most scrutinized domestic portraits ever painted.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, flemish, symbolic, domestic, van eyck, double portrait
items.credit_line: Web site of National Gallery, London

items.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
items.description_narrative: Georges Seurat's monumental oil on canvas, "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884," captures Parisians enjoying a leisurely afternoon on an island in the Seine. This iconic work is meticulously composed using the artist's groundbreaking pointillist technique, creating luminous color and form.
items.tags: sunday, leisure, park, pointillism, post-impressionism, Parisian life, serene, vibrant

items.title: Café Terrace at Night
items.description_narrative: A warmly lit café terrace on the Place du Forum in Arles, France, under a deep blue starry sky. One of Van Gogh's first paintings to feature his signature nocturnal sky, it contrasts the warm golden gaslight with the cool blues of the evening.
items.tags: cafe, night, stars, arles, post-impressionism, urban

items.title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
items.description_narrative: Painted at dusk along the riverbank at Arles, van Gogh set gaslit town lights and the stars of Ursa Major shimmering above the Rhône's rippling reflections. It was one of several night scenes he made the year before his more famous Starry Night.
items.tags: van gogh, arles, rhone river, night sky, stars, post-impressionism, reflections

items.title: Wheatfield with Cypresses
items.description_narrative: Painted near the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, this canvas pairs a wind-tossed wheatfield with dark flame-like cypress trees Van Gogh described as 'beautiful in line and proportion, like an Egyptian obelisk.' He made several versions of the composition; this one is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.title: The School of Athens
items.description_narrative: A fresco in the Apostolic Palace in the Vatican depicting a congregation of the greatest philosophers, mathematicians, and scientists of antiquity, with Plato and Aristotle at the center. It is considered a masterpiece of perspective and one of the greatest achievements of Renaissance art.
items.tags: philosophy, plato, aristotle, fresco, renaissance, architecture
items.credit_line: "School of Athens" by Raphael, Raphael Rooms, Vatican Museum Complete indexed photo collection at WorldHistoryPics.com.

items.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
items.description_narrative: Bacchus leaps from his chariot toward the abandoned Ariadne in a whirl of leopards, satyrs, and brilliant ultramarine sky. Painted for the Duke of Ferrara's private study, it remains one of the most vividly colored mythological scenes of the Italian Renaissance.
items.tags: renaissance, mythology, venetian, dynamic, colorful, titian, movement
items.credit_line: Own work Joyofmuseums Taken on 16 July 2018

items.title: Virgin of the Rocks
items.medium: Oil on panel, transferred to canvas
items.description_narrative: The Louvre's version of Leonardo's altarpiece, one of two nearly identical compositions he painted, showing the Virgin, the infant Christ, the young John the Baptist, and an angel in a shadowy grotto. It is a defining demonstration of Leonardo's sfumato technique, with figures modeled in soft gradations of light and shade rather than hard outlines.

items.title: The Raft of the Medusa
items.description_narrative: Géricault based this monumental shipwreck scene on a real 1816 disaster in which survivors of the frigate Méduse drifted for thirteen days on a makeshift raft, resorting to starvation and mutiny. Its raw depiction of suffering and political scandal made it an inaugural masterpiece of French Romanticism.
items.tags: gericault, shipwreck, raft, romanticism, disaster, survival, french painting
